correctness.rationale: Reconstructed unique stationary perpetuity from Poisson last-reset Gaussian mixture; verified Laplace innovation transform and centered tail variance 2c²/[λ²(1−c²)]. The inner expansion uses uniform second-moment control and exact Laplace E|y−W| identity. The outer expansion uses exponential tails of the small residual. Distributional Laplace second derivative gives μ0−δ0. Upper TV follows the L1 second-translation inequality using ||p0″||var=2λ²; lower TV follows tail event {|x|>epsilon}, cosh expansion, and epsilon↓0. Finite checker exercises normalized partial fractions, characteristic products and finite TV bounds; analytical limits do not depend on finite truncation. For the additional density-crossing claim, p_c/p_0 is strictly increasing in the positive spatial coordinate, from E exp(-λ|Z_c|)<1 to E exp(λZ_c)>1. The exact partial-fraction density expansion has leading n=0,1 terms and a uniformly O(c^4 exp[-λx(1/c²−1)]) remainder; comparison at x=(1±eta)c log(1/c)/λ proves the unique logarithmic crossing scale.

value.rationale: At fixed nonzero contraction the reset-point stationary density is rounded, whereas full resetting has a Laplace cusp. The theorem quantifies a singular crossover with a universal width-c layer, isolates the disappearing central mass as a Dirac defect at the c² scale, proves that all macroscopic spatial locations gain the same proportional leading density, and computes the operationally relevant supremum probability discrepancy exactly. These are motivated transport/inference consequences of the physical complete-vs-partial-reset limit, not arbitrary parameter slices or recomputations of known moments. The single optimal distinguishing region and its intermediate c log(1/c) boundary supply an exact testing interpretation and reveal a scale invisible in either fixed-position or fixed-inner-coordinate limits.
